title: String Comparison
prompt:
Compare two strings using comparison operators
Sample Input: Hello, World
Sample Output: true, false
answer:
Sure, I'd be happy to help you with that! When comparing two strings using comparison operators in most programming languages, the result is a boolean value (true or false). Here's how you can compare two strings using comparison operators in some popular programming languages:

1. JavaScript:

```javascript
let str1 = "Hello, World";
let str2 = "Hello, World";

console.log(str1 === str2); // true
console.log(str1 == str2); // true
console.log(str1 != str2); // false
console.log(str1 < str2); // false
console.log(str1 > str2); // false
console.log(str1 <= str2); // false
console.log(str1 >= str2); // false
```

2. Python:

```python
str1 = "Hello, World"
str2 = "Hello, World"

print(str1 == str2)  # True
print(str1 != str2)  # False
print(str1 < str2)   # False
print(str1 > str2)   # False
print(str1 <= str2)  # False
print(str1 >= str2)  # False
```

3. Java:

```java
String str1 = "Hello, World";
String str2 = "Hello, World";

System.out.println(str1 == str2); // true
System.out.println(str1 != str2); // false
System.out.println(str1 < str2); // false
System.out.println(str1 > str2); // false
System.out.println(str1 <= str2); // false
System.out.println(str1 >= str2); // false
```

4. C# (using string comparison operators):

```csharp
string str1 = "Hello, World";
string str2 = "Hello, World";

Console.WriteLine(str1 == str2); // true
Console.WriteLine(str1 != str2); // false
Console.WriteLine(str1 < str2); // false
Console.WriteLine(str1 > str2); // false
Console.WriteLine(str1 <= str2); // false
Console.WriteLine(str1 >= str2); // false
```

5. C++ (using string comparison operators):

```cpp
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    std::string str1 = "Hello, World";
    std::string str2 = "Hello, World";

    std::cout << (str1 == str2) << std::endl; // true
    std::cout << (str1 != str2) << std::endl; // false
    std::cout << (str1 < str2) << std::endl; // false
    std::cout << (str1 > str2) << std::endl; // false
    std::cout << (str1 <= str2) << std::endl; // false
    std::cout << (str1 >= str2) << std::endl; // false

    return 0;
}
```
